newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip on Hebron deal hopes.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip on Hebron deal hopes.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cancelled a trip to the United States on Wednesday only hours before he was set to leave as Israeli and PLO negotiators struggled to sew up a deal on Hebron.

"That's correct," a spokeswoman in Netanyahu's office said when asked to confirm reports by Israel's Channel One and Channel Two television stations that Netanyhahu had cancelled his trip. Netanyahu was to have left late on Wednesday.
Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel, told Reuters of Netanyahu's decision: "He doesn't want his visit to in any way delay arriving at a successful agreement."
Asked if a deal might be clinched on Wednesday night, an Israeli official who spoke on condition he not be named said: "It's possible but it's also possible it will happen tomorrow."
Negotiators are trying to close the deal under which Israeli troops would hand over 80 percent of the volatile West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian police.

They broke from talks at mid-day. Two Palestinian negotiators met Netanyahu in Tel Aviv on Wednesday night. They then headed for the home of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk near Tel Aviv to resume negotiations.
"We met with Mr Netanyahu and we discussed all issues in general without getting into the details," top Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, said.
"We discussed the need to move forward and the dangers of any delay and the need for both sides to make an effort to reach an agreement," he told Reuters.

Fogel told reporters earlier in the day in Hebron that Netanyahu, who had been due to speak to Jewish supporters in the United States, would postpone the trip if an agreement was close. The trip would have been his fourth to the United States in five months in power.

Palestinian officials said after the earlier talks on Wednesday that the sides were stalemated over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to enter Palestinian-controlled parts of Hebron in "hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.
But Fogel said the sides had achieved "significant progress" and were trying to define how Israeli forces might operate against what he called "terrorists" in Palestinian-run areas.

"They are actually trying to formulate in writing the bounds and limits and ways the Israeli military will be allowed to act in areas of control of the Palestinian Authority," Fogel said of the talks.
PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat held three hours of intensive talks with Netanyahu's personal adviser, attorney Yitzhak Molho, on Wednesday.
Netanyahu wants to modify the Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous government to safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in guarded enclaves among 100,000 Arabs.
The Hebron pullout was due last March but was delayed after Moslem militant suicide bomb attacks in Israel.
